name: Respond to a webhook
description: Learn how a Webhook trigger starts a workflow from an HTTP request and how the workflow answers the caller. Send a name with curl, see the request in the trigger's output, and the workflow builds a JSON greeting as the response. It needs no connection.
shortDescription: Learn how a Webhook trigger starts a workflow from an HTTP request and how the workflow answers the caller.
keyFeatures: Start a workflow from any app with an HTTP request to its webhook URL
Capture a sample request with Test Trigger and run the workflow on it
Answer the caller with a JSON response built from the request
Fall back to a default value in a formula when a field is missing
idealFor: First-time ByteChef users who want to learn how other apps can start a workflow and get an answer back.
steps: Trigger: the workflow starts when an HTTP request arrives at its webhook URL, and the caller waits for the answer.
Log the request: the Logger writes the JSON body the caller sent.
Send a greeting back: the workflow answers with status 200 and {"greeting": "Hello, <name>!"}, or "Hello, there!" when no name was sent.
